<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The script `thorium-cpu-check.sh` is a CPU feature detection and compatibility checker for the Thorium Browser Beta package. It reads `/proc/cpuinfo` to determine supported CPU instruction sets and checks whether the currently installed package (e.g., `thorium-browser-beta-sse4-bin`) is compatible with the host's CPU architecture. It supports multiple variants (SSE4, AVX, AVX2, AVX-512) and selects the best available package variant based on CPU capabilities.

The script performs no network operations, file modifications, or system installations. It only outputs warnings via `stderr` or `notify-send` when running in `runtime` mode, and these notifications are limited to compatibility advisories. The use of `notify-send` is gated on the presence of a display server and runs asynchronously without capturing output or affecting system state. All operations are local, transparent, and consistent with safe runtime environment checks.

There is no obfuscation, code execution, or data exfiltration. The script respects build-time conditions (e.g., skipping checks on packaging servers) and follows standard shell scripting practices with strict error handling (`set -euo pipefail`). Its behavior is entirely aligned with the expected functionality of a CPU compatibility verifier for a performance-optimized browser package.
</details>
<evidence>
